subject: chemistry
title: Ceramics, polymers and composites
key_idea: Glass and clay ceramics are made by heating. Thermosoftening polymers melt, while thermosetting polymers have cross-links and do not. A composite has a matrix binding a reinforcement. Materials are chosen by matching their properties to the use. (Separate science)

blocks.text: Glass and clay ceramics are made by heating. This section covers how each is made and what they are like.

items.meaning: A material such as pottery or brick, made by shaping wet clay and then heating it in a furnace.
The glass most often used. It is made by heating sand, sodium carbonate and limestone.
Glass made from sand and boron trioxide. It melts at a higher temperature than soda-lime glass.

items: Soda-lime glass: heat a mixture of sand, sodium carbonate and limestone.
Borosilicate glass: made from sand and boron trioxide, and it melts at higher temperatures.
Clay ceramics, including pottery and bricks: shape wet clay, then heat it in a furnace.
Glass and clay ceramics have a high melting point, low flexibility and do not react with water.
They are poor conductors of electricity.
Soda-lime glass is made from sand, sodium carbonate and limestone.
Clay ceramics are shaped when wet, then heated in a furnace.
Glass and ceramics have high melting points and do not react with water.

blocks.text: The properties of a polymer depend on the monomers it is made from and the conditions it is made under. This section compares two kinds of polymer.

items: Low density (LD) and high density (HD) poly(ethene) are both produced from ethene.
They have different properties because they are made under different conditions, such as different temperatures and pressures.

items.meaning: A polymer that melts when it is heated.
A polymer that does not melt when it is heated.

rows: Long chains with covalent bonds (cross-links) between the chains
Does not melt, because too much energy is needed to overcome the cross-links
Easier, because it melts and can be reshaped into new products
Harder, because it does not melt

diagram.alt: Sort statements into thermosoftening and thermosetting polymers.
diagram.prompt: Which kind of polymer does each statement describe?

items: Polymer properties depend on the monomers and the conditions they are made under.
Thermosoftening polymers melt. Thermosetting polymers do not.
Thermosetting polymers have cross-links between chains.

blocks.text: A composite combines two materials to give properties neither has alone. This section covers how a composite is made up.

items.meaning: The material that surrounds and binds together the fibres or fragments.
The fibres or fragments of the other material in a composite.

items: Most composites are made of two materials.
The matrix or binder surrounds and binds together the reinforcement.
Example: a composite of carbon fibre (reinforcement) in a polymer resin (matrix).
Pre-stressed concrete is stronger than plain concrete, so it is used for bridges that carry heavy lorries.
A composite has a matrix (binder) and a reinforcement.
The matrix surrounds and binds the fibres or fragments.

sections.heading: Choosing a material for a use (Separate science)

blocks.text: Questions give a table of data and ask which material suits a use. Compare the values, then link each property to the use.

items: Write the property, then the reason it matters, such as high melting point so a cup will not melt.
A high density makes an object heavier, so a low density suits something carried or worn.
A strong material is less likely to break or be damaged.
A stiff material is less likely to bend out of shape.
A polymer is chosen to insulate a household wire because it does not conduct electricity and it is flexible. The wire inside is metal because a metal conducts electricity.
A metal is chosen for a pan base because it conducts heat well and its melting point is high enough.
Compare the data. Do not only quote values from the table.
Link each property to a reason it matters for the use.
End an evaluation with a justified conclusion.

checks.q: Name the three materials heated to make soda-lime glass.
Explain why some polymers do not melt when heated.
checks.a: There are cross-links, or covalent bonds, between the polymer chains. Too much energy is needed to overcome them.

checks.q: Explain why poly(ethene) is easier to recycle than thermosetting polymers.
checks.a: Poly(ethene) melts, so it can be reshaped into new products.

exam_phrases: with covalent bonds between the chains
too much energy needed to overcome the cross-links
melts so can be reshaped (into new products)
(wet) clay is shaped and heated in a furnace

mistakes.wrong: Thermosetting polymers do not melt because the intermolecular forces between chains are strong.
mistakes.right: References to intermolecular forces are ignored. There are covalent bonds (cross-links) between the chains, so too much energy is needed to overcome them.

mistakes.wrong: Pre-stressed concrete is used for bridges because it is more dense.
mistakes.right: More dense is not accepted. It is stronger, so it can bear the weight of heavy traffic.

mistakes.wrong: The outer coating on a surfboard is added to stop the board rusting.
mistakes.right: References to corrosion or rusting are ignored. Say the coating makes the board stronger, harder, tougher or waterproof.

worked_example.question:
Materials could be used to make badminton racket frames.

The table shows properties of three materials.

| Material | Density (g/cm3) | Relative strength | Relative stiffness |
| Aluminium | 2.7 | 0.3 | 69 |
| Carbon nanotube | 1.5 | 60 | 1000 |
| Wood | 0.71 | 0.1 | 10 |

Evaluate the use of the materials to make badminton racket frames.

Use the table.
answer_points: Wood is the least dense, so it is the lightest to use.
Aluminium is the most dense, so it will make the racket too heavy.
Carbon nanotube is the strongest, so it is least likely to break. Wood and aluminium are too weak, so the racket would break more easily.
Carbon nanotube is the stiffest, so it is least likely to bend out of shape.
worked_example.tip: Marked in levels: logically linked reasons and a simple judgement reach the top level for 4 marks.

mistakes.wrong: The ceramic is suitable because it is a good material for a cup.
mistakes.right: No property given means no marks. Give a correct property from the data, such as high melting point, and link it to a reason, such as the cup will not melt or distort.

mistakes.wrong: A metal is the most suitable material for the insulation on a household wire.
mistakes.right: A metal conducts electricity, so it is not an insulator. The polymer is the most suitable, because it has low electrical conductivity and is flexible.

mistakes.wrong: The wire is made of metal because metals are hard.
mistakes.right: Metals are not hard (their hardness is low). The wire is made of metal because the metal conducts electricity.

worked_example.question:
The table shows information about a glass, a ceramic, a polymer and a metal.

| | glass | ceramic | polymer | metal |
| flexibility | low | low | high | high |
| hardness | medium | medium | low | low |
| reaction with water | no reaction | no reaction | no reaction | very slow reaction |
| electrical conductivity | low | low | low | high |
| melting point | high | high | medium* | high |

*polymers soften, rather than melt, when heated.

Explain, using information from the table, why the ceramic is a suitable material to make a cup that will contain a hot drink of tea or coffee.
answer_points: A correct property: it does not react with water, or has a high melting point, or low flexibility.
Linked to a reason: drinks contain water, so it will not react with the drink.
Or: the ceramic will not melt, or the cup will not distort and will keep its shape.
worked_example.tip: Mark one property and its linked reason. Incorrect extra properties are ignored.

exam_phrases: lower density so easier to wear or carry
does not corrode so it will last longer

mistakes.wrong: Polymer B should be used because it has a high melting point.
mistakes.right: A high melting point is ignored unless qualified. Say it will not melt or soften when filled with a hot drink, so it holds its shape.

mistakes.wrong: Kevlar is used for vests because it is better at keeping you safe.
mistakes.right: This is ignored. Describe a property and explain it, such as stronger so less likely to be penetrated, or lower density so more comfortable to wear.

mistakes.wrong: Metal is used for the base of a pan because it conducts heat well.
mistakes.right: Conducts heat well is ignored. Say it has the highest thermal conductivity, and a suitable high melting point.

worked_example.question:
The table shows information about three different polymers, A, B and C.

Tensile strength is the amount of load a material can take before it breaks.

| Polymer | Melting point (°C) | Softening temperature (°C) | Stiffness (MPa) | Tensile strength (MPa) |
| A | 130 | 72 | 980 | 15 |
| B | 240 | 95 | 3200 | 65 |
| C | 250 | 75 | 2400 | 50 |

A company wants to use a polymer to make a disposable cup for hot drinks.

Suggest and explain which polymer, A, B or C, the company should use.
answer_points: B will not soften when filled with a hot drink, so it will hold its shape.
B will not melt when filled with a hot drink.
worked_example.tip: One mark for B, then any two reasons. The mark is for the reason, not just quoting a table value.
